k:multilingual-eval-faq@1.1:e2ea02bf.excerpt:
## Tool issues

### Q: Characters or tone marks appear as boxes or become unreadable in LT.
Report a tool-rendering incident and check the text outside LT where possible. Until that comparison is available, do not claim the underlying response itself has corrupted characters.

k:multilingual-eval-instructions@1.2:ea9.excerpt:
## Tool incidents and submission
Boxes, missing diacritics or broken characters in LT are tool-rendering incidents until the source text is checked. Compare outside the tool where possible. If unavailable, record the limitation rather than asserting that the model produced corrupt text.

Capture task IDs for rendering or submission failures. Treat tool impact under the operational incident rubric, separately from language-quality grades. A saved rating is not proof of a completed submission.

k:multilingual-eval-instructions@1.2:818.excerpt:
## Project purpose
Evaluate language adherence, register consistency, naturalness and regional appropriateness against the intended audience. Distinguish linguistic defects from tool rendering failures.

# Korean register case referred to language QA

## Request
M10-KO-017 contains a polite narrative followed by a casual sentence inside quotation marks. The packet did not identify whether the quoted speaker and addressee changed.

## TL decision
Alex routed the case to Hana (U008), whose recorded specialty is Korean, with the exact endings and surrounding paragraph. Do not assign a major register penalty from the ending change alone.

## Requested assessment
Establish who is speaking, whether the quote is intentional, and whether the language remains appropriate for the intended audience. The original scoring question stays open until that context is reviewed.

## Scope
This referral concerns M10-KO-017 in batch 10. It is not a general exemption for Korean register shifts.
